definitions.explanation: A vivid, deep red color. Originally referred to the dye extracted from safflower (紅花). A literary and poetic word for red.

examples.japanese: {紅|くれない}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{染|そ}まる→染まる：04254_somaru⟧。
⟦{夕焼|ゆうや}け→夕焼け：05045_yuuyake⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{空|そら}→空：02216_sora⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{紅|くれない}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{染|そ}めた→染める：04253_someru⟧。
examples.english: The sunset dyed the sky crimson.

examples.japanese: ⟦{秋|あき}→秋：02276_aki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{山|やま}→山：02168_yama⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{木々|きぎ}→木々：04811_kigi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{紅|くれない}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{色|いろ}づき→色づく：10074_irozuku⟧、⟦{美|うつく}しい→美しい：01121_utsukushii⟧⟦{風景|ふうけい}→風景：03591_fuukei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{広|ひろ}がる→広がる：01980_hirogaru⟧。
examples.english: In autumn, the mountain trees turn crimson, creating a beautiful landscape.

notes:
A literary and elegant word for a deep, vivid red. The character {紅|くれない} can also be read as べ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ (lipstick, rouge) — a separate entry — but ⟦くれない→くれる：00724_kureru⟧ specifically refers to the color itself with a poetic nuance.

ETYMOLOGY:
Derived from the dye produced from {紅花|べにばな} (safflower), which was historically imported via China. The word ⟦くれない→くれる：00724_kureru⟧ is thought to come from {呉|くれ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{藍|あい}→藍：20100_ai⟧ (indigo/dye from the kingdom of Wu), referring to the Chinese origin of the dyeing technique.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {紅|くれない}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{染|そ}まる→染まる：04254_somaru⟧: to turn crimson
- {紅|くれない}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{色|いろ}づく→色づく：10074_irozuku⟧: to take on a crimson hue
- {紅|くれない}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{涙|なみだ}→涙：02235_namida⟧: crimson tears (literary)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{赤|あか}→赤：02842_aka⟧: red — the everyday, general-purpose word for red
- べ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ (⟦{紅|べに}→紅：13862_beni⟧): rouge, lipstick — the cosmetic reading of the same character
- {緋|ひ}: scarlet — a brighter, more orange-tinged red
